answer: Bonded identity deposits raise the sybil tax: every new agent must lock refundable stake before it can act, and that bond is no velvet shortcut. Forging a fleet forces an attacker to post an atlas of separate deposits, each independently slashable. One whisper of coordinated collusion, caught by peer attestation, burns every linked bond at once, so minting thousands of identities costs real locked capital, not just cheap compute.
